# Theorem L: all-orders proof (proof of record = R3 proof (ii))

Status tags: [P] proved here; [C] cited; [E] evidence only (no proof step uses it).

Notation. sigma = tau(1+tau). Pi_k = prod_{a=1}^{k-1}(k tau+a)/(k-1)!, so Pi_1 = 1, and Pi_k != 0 in Q[tau]. For a multiset U of positive integers: r_U = #U, J_U = Sum u, D_U = J_U - r_U. delta_g(U) = D_U - 2g + 2. (a)_k = a(a-1)...(a-k+1). All identities hold over the field Q(tau); nothing is specialised until the last line of s.5.

## 0. Why (ii)

Proof (ii) needs only (MV), the members P_k and the dilaton calculus, all written below. Proof (i) would add a citation (MV cut-and-join) or KP. In the proof below the empty-profile table, the additive-constant issue and the v = 0 issue disappear, because every Hirota block is differentiated at least once and unit parts are treated like other parts.

## 1. Named input MVmatch [C]

(MV) In Q[tau]((x))[[p_1,p_2,...]], with q = e^x, p_k(q^rho) = 1/(q^{k/2}-q^{-k/2}), f_2(nu) = sum of contents, and Z(p) := Sum_nu e^{tau x f_2(nu)} s_nu(q^rho) s_nu(p):

log Z = Sum_{mu != empty} Sum_{g>=0} x^{2g-2+l(mu)} sigma^{g+l(mu)-1} Pi_mu M_g(mu) p_mu/|Aut mu|,

where M_g(mu) = Int_{Mbar_{g,l}} Omega_g prod 1/(1-mu_i psi_i), Pi_mu = prod Pi_{mu_i}, and M_0(mu) := |mu|^{l-3} for all l >= 1. This is the LLZ convention for l = 1, 2. For l >= 3 it is the multinomial formula <tau_{d_1}...tau_{d_l}>_0 = (l-3)!/prod d_i!.

This is the only form of the MV formula used.

Derivation from LLZ (arXiv math/0306434v3), for the MVmatch owner to check. LLZ (1)-(3) read Sum lambda^{2g-2+l} C_{g,mu} p_mu = log Sum_nu e^{i(tau+1/2)kappa_nu lambda/2} V_nu s_nu(p), with
- C_{g,mu} = -(i^{|mu|+l}/|Aut mu|) sigma^{l-1} Pi_mu I_g(mu), where I_g = (-sigma)^g M_g;
- V_nu = prod_box 1/(2 sin(h lambda/2)), from (3) and (8). The printed Prop. 2.1 has "2^l" where (3) gives 2^{|nu|}.
Put x = i lambda and p^_k = i^k p_k. Then 2 sin(h lambda/2) = [h]/i with [h] = q^{h/2}-q^{-h/2}, so V_nu s_nu(p) = s_nu(p^)/prod[h]. Moreover s_nu(q^rho) = q^{kappa/4}/prod[h] and kappa = 2 f_2, so the right side is log Z(p^). On the left, lambda^{2g-2+l} C_{g,mu} p_mu = (-1)^{g-1} (-i)^l x^{2g-2+l} (-i^{l}) sigma^{l-1} Pi_mu I_g p^_mu/|Aut mu| = (-1)^g sigma^{l-1} Pi_mu I_g x^{2g-2+l} p^_mu/|Aut mu|. Finally (-1)^g I_g = sigma^g M_g gives (MV). The earlier notes omit the factor i^{|mu|} and use [h] in place of 2 sin; the two forms are related exactly by p -> p^.

Variables. Over Q(tau) set hbar = sigma x^2, y = q_1 = x sigma p_1, q_k = x sigma Pi_k p_k (k >= 2). For a multiset U of positive integers put G^(g)_U(y) := Sum_{a>=0} M_g(U+1^a) y^a/a! (U non-empty, or U empty with g >= 2). Then (MV) reads

F := log Z = Sum_g hbar^{g-1} F_g, with F_g = Sum_{T, parts>=2} q_T G^(g)_T/|Aut T| and the a = 0 term omitted when T is empty. (1.1)

## 2. The members P_k, for all k [P]

Conventions (the same as Jimbo-Miwa s.1 and Harnad-Orlov (5.3)):
- psi_i, psi*_i act on semi-infinite wedges, with psi_i = e_i wedge and psi*_i = d/de_i. |n> = e_{n-1} wedge e_{n-2} wedge ..., and |nu,n> has occupied modes nu_j + n - j.
- alpha_k = Sum_j :psi_j psi*_{j+k}:. Then [alpha_k,psi_i] = psi_{i-k}, [alpha_k,psi*_i] = -psi*_{i+k}, [alpha_k,alpha_l] = k delta_{k+l}, alpha_k|n> = 0 and <n|alpha_{-k} = 0 for k > 0.
- H(t) = Sum_{k>=1} t_k alpha_k, Gamma(t') = exp(Sum t'_k alpha_{-k}), with p_k = k t_k throughout. xi(t,z) = Sum t_k z^k, [1/z]_k = z^{-k}/k.

(F1) alpha_{-k} moves one particle up by k with sign (-1)^{height}. So Murnaghan-Nakayama and Frobenius give <n|e^{H(t)}|nu,n> = s_nu(t) and Gamma(t')|n> = Sum_nu s_nu(t')|nu,n>. Since the character table is invertible, F_n is spanned by the alpha_{-mu}|n>.

(F2) Let W be the diagonal operator with W|S> = B^{Lambda(S)}|S>, where Lambda(S) = Sum_{j in S, j>=0} f(j) - Sum_{j not in S, j<0} f(j) and f(j) = j(j+1)/2. Then W psi_i W^{-1} = B^{f(i)} psi_i and W psi*_i W^{-1} = B^{-f(i)} psi*_i. Also Lambda(|nu,n>) = f_2(nu) + n|nu| + a_n, because f(nu_j+n-j) - f(n-j) = nu_j(nu_j-2j+1)/2 + n nu_j. Here a_0 = a_1 = 0.

Hence, with G := W Gamma(t'), for n = 0, 1:
tau_n(t) := <n|e^{H(t)} G|n> = Sum_nu B^{f_2(nu)+n|nu|} s_nu(t') s_nu(t).
So tau_0 = Z(p) and tau_1 = Z(e^{beta} o p) := Z((e^{k beta} p_k)_k) at B = e^{beta}, beta = tau x, t' = q^rho. No normalising constant occurs.

(F3) S := Sum_i psi_i tensor psi*_i is a finite sum on any v tensor v' of wedges. It commutes with G tensor G: termwise for W by (F2), and for Gamma because Sum_i ([alpha_{-k},psi_i] tensor psi*_i + psi_i tensor [alpha_{-k},psi*_i]) = Sum_i (psi_{i+k} tensor psi*_i - psi_i tensor psi*_{i-k}) = 0.

On |0> tensor |1> only i = 0 survives, and S(|0> tensor |1>) = |1> tensor |0>. So S(G|0> tensor G|1>) = G|1> tensor G|0>.

(F4) With psi(z) = Sum psi_i z^i and psi*(z) = Sum psi*_i z^{-i}: [alpha_k,psi(z)] = z^k psi(z) and [alpha_k,psi*(z)] = -z^k psi*(z), so e^{H(t)} psi(z) = e^{xi(t,z)} psi(z) e^{H(t)} and e^{H(t)} psi*(z) = e^{-xi(t,z)} psi*(z) e^{H(t)}.

The covector <1|psi(z) on F_0 is an eigenvector of right multiplication by alpha_{-k} with eigenvalue -z^{-k}, and takes the value 1 on |0>. The covector <0|e^{H(-[1/z])} has the same two properties. By (F1), <1|psi(z) = <0|e^{H(-[1/z])}. Likewise <0|psi*(z) = <1|e^{H([1/z])} on F_1 (eigenvalue +z^{-k}, value 1 on |1>).

(F5) Pair (F3) with <1|e^{H(t)} tensor <0|e^{H(t~)} and use (F4):

[z^0] e^{xi(t-t~,z)} tau_0(t-[1/z]) tau_1(t~+[1/z]) = tau_1(t) tau_0(t~). (2.1)

At fixed degrees in t, t~, t' every sum is finite. Coefficients lie in Q[B^{+-1}, t'], so the specialisation B = e^{tau x}, t' = q^rho is legitimate coefficientwise.

(F6) Put t = T+u, t~ = T-u. Writing tau_0(T+a) tau_1(T-a) = exp(Sum a_k D_k) tau_0.tau_1, with D_k the Hirota derivative in T_k, (2.1) becomes

Sum_{j>=0} p_j(2u) p_j(-D~) exp(Sum u_k D_k) tau_0.tau_1 = exp(-Sum u_k D_k) tau_0.tau_1,

where e^{xi(t,z)} = Sum p_j(t) z^j and D~ = (D_k/k). Since p_j(2u) = 2 u_j + (terms of degree >= 2 in u), the u_k-linear part at u = 0 is D_k + 2 p_k(-D~) = -D_k. That is:

**P_k(D) tau_0.tau_1 = 0, with P_k := D_k + p_k(-D~), for every k >= 1.** (2.2)

Explicitly P_k = Sum_{alpha |- k} c_alpha D^alpha, with c_alpha = prod_i (-1/i)^{m_i}/m_i! + [alpha=(k)]. So c_(k) = 1 - 1/k, which is non-zero for k >= 2. Examples: 2P_2 = D_1^2 + D_2; 6P_3 = 4D_3 + 3D_1D_2 - D_1^3; 24P_4 = D_1^4 + 8D_1D_3 - 6D_1^2D_2 + 3D_2^2 + 18D_4. This fixes the form for all k and the orientation tau_1 = Z(e^{+tau x} o p); no finite check enters.

## 3. Dilaton calculus [P]

Let u be a formal variable, y = u e^{-u}, w = 1/(1-u) (so u = T(y) is the tree function), D = y d/dy = (w-1) d/du and d/du w^n = n w^{n+1}. Let L_J := e^{uJ} Q(tau)[w,1/w], a subset of Q(tau)[[u]].

Lemma 3.1 (operators).
(J+D)(e^{uJ} w^n) = e^{uJ}((J-n) w^{n+1} + n w^{n+2}).
d/dy (e^{uJ} w^n) = e^{u(J+1)}(J w^{n+1} + n w^{n+2}), using 1/y = e^u w/(w-1).
Also d/dy D = (D+1) d/dy. Direct computation.

Lemma 3.2 (Route A Prop 2.1 / Cor 2.2). Let g >= 1 with U non-empty, or g >= 2 with U empty; parts >= 1. Put r = r_U, J = J_U, N = 3g-3+r, and Q_g(s;U) := Sum_m (s^m/m!) <Omega_g prod lam_j (psi^2/(1-psi))^{tensor m}>. This has degree <= N in s, because each leaf has psi-degree >= 2. Then

G^(g)_U(u e^{-u}) = e^{uJ} w^{2g-2+r} Q_g(w-1;U), and X_g(U) := Q_g(-1;U) = Xi_g(U). (3.1)

Proof.
- Write psi^2/(1-psi) = lam_1 - 1 - psi with lam_1 = 1/(1-psi), and expand: Q = Sum_{a,b,c} s^{a+b+c} (-1)^{b+c}/(a! b! c!) <lam_U lam_1^a 1^b psi^c>.
- Omega pulls back under forgetful maps, so the dilaton equation removes the c psi's with factor (e)^(c) (rising factorial), e = 2g-2+r+a+b.
- The string equation pi_* prod lam_{j_i} = (Sum j_i) prod lam_{j_i} removes the b constants with factor (J+a)^b.
- Sum over c: (1+s)^{-e}. Sum over b: exp(-s(J+a)/(1+s)). So Q = (1+s)^{-(2g-2+r)} e^{-uJ} Sum_a (u e^{-u})^a M_g(U+1^a)/a!, with u = s/(1+s), 1+s = w. All stability conditions hold since r+a >= 1 when g = 1. QED.
Xi_g(U) = Q_g(-1;U) is the definition, as T = -psi^2/(1-psi). The K-form is the standard pushforward: with s_a = s, 1 - s w/(1-w) = (1-(1+s)w)/(1-w) gives K_s = exp(Sum((1+s)^k-1) kappa_k/k).

Lemma 3.3 (genus 0; Route A Lemma 3.1). For U non-empty with parts >= 1, r = r_U, J = J_U: e^{-uJ} G^(0)_U = w^{r-2}·(polynomial in w) with constant term X_0(U) := Gamma(J)/Gamma(J-r+3).

Proof. G^(0)_U = Sum_a (J+a)^{a+r-3} y^a/a!, and (J+D) multiplies the coefficient of y^a by J+a. So (J+D) is injective on power series, and it raises r-3 by one. By Lagrange inversion, Sum_a (J+a)^{a-1} y^a/a! = e^{uJ}/J, which is r = 2. Lemma 3.1 gives r >= 3, with leading coefficient prod_{n=1}^{r-3}(J-n). For r = 1 the solution of (J+D)G = e^{uJ}/J is e^{uJ}(w^{-1}/(J(J+1)) + 1/(J^2(J+1))), as checked by Lemma 3.1. QED.

Lemma 3.4 (uniform leading coefficient; replaces R3 Lemmas 2.1 and 2.3). For all g >= 0, k >= 0 and U NON-EMPTY with parts >= 1:

NOTATION. eps := e1 e2 of the draft (eps1 eps2), E := eps1 + eps2 (the weight). E(y) is BS's function, written with its argument to avoid the clash. a_d := (3d)!/(d!)^3, H_n harmonic, Delta_c := 1+27y, X := 1/Delta_c, L2b := theta^2 + 3y(3theta+1)(3theta+2) = Delta_c theta^2 + 27y theta + 6y.

=== PART I. PROOF OF THEOREM 1. All steps [P]; no citation, no GW input, no finite-order step. ===

Step 0 (read off eq:Ifun). With s = 1/z, the d-th summand (d >= 1) of I/(z y^{H/z}) is
  y^d Prod_{m=0}^{3d-1}(-m-3Hs) / Prod_j Prod_{m=1}^d (m+(H+alpha_j)s)
  = 3H (-y)^d (3d-1)!/(d!)^3 s [1 + s(3H H_{3d-1} - (3H+e_1(alpha)) H_d) + O(s^2)].
Multiplying by z y^{H/z} and using 3d(3d-1)! = (3d)! gives:
  A = Sum a_d (-y)^d,
  G := theta I_1^[1]/e_1(alpha) = -Sum a_d H_d (-y)^d,
  P := theta I_1^[2] = A log y + h,  h := Sum 3 a_d (H_{3d}-H_d)(-y)^d.
(For h: the term from I_0^[1] contributes (a_d/d)(-y)^d, and 1/d + 3H_{3d-1} = 3H_{3d}.) So E(y) = theta(G/A), D = theta(P/A), and E(y) does not depend on alpha. No reduction mod the cubic relation occurs at this order. This agrees with eq:Ian.

Step 1 (L2b on series). For phi = Sum phi_d (-y)^d,
  [(-y)^d] L2b phi = d^2 phi_d - 3(3d-1)(3d-2) phi_{d-1}.
Since d^2 a_d = 3(3d-1)(3d-2) a_{d-1}:
  (i) L2b A = 0;
  (ii) if phi_d = a_d g_d then [(-y)^d] L2b phi = d^2 a_d (g_d - g_{d-1});
  (iii) L2b is injective on y Q[[y]], because the lowest term d >= 1 has coefficient d^2 phi_d != 0.
Product rule: L2b(A l) = Delta_c(2 thetaA thetal + A theta^2 l) + 27y A thetal.

Step 2 (key identity). Sum_d a_d (3H_{3d} - H_d)(-y)^d = -A log(1+27y).  (K)
Both sides lie in y Q[[y]]. For the left side, g_d = 3H_{3d} - H_d gives g_d - g_{d-1} = 3/(3d-1) + 3/(3d-2) = 9(2d-1)/((3d-1)(3d-2)), so by (ii) the (-y)^d coefficient of L2b is 27(2d-1) a_{d-1}. For the right side, theta log Delta_c = 27yX and theta^2 log Delta_c = 27yX^2, so the product rule gives L2b(A log Delta_c) = 54y thetaA + 27y A, whose (-y)^d coefficient is -27(2d-1) a_{d-1}. Hence L2b of the right side has the same coefficient. Apply (iii).
Comparing coefficients in (K), after dividing by 27^d, is exactly eq:limitconv.

Step 3 (eq:DEXrel). 2G - h = -Sum a_d (3H_{3d}-H_d)(-y)^d = A log Delta_c by (K). So 2G - P + A log(y/Delta_c) = 0, which is eq:DEXrel.

Step 4 (second relation). Divide by A: G/A = (P/A - l)/2 with l = log(y/Delta_c). Since theta l = 1 - 27yX = X, applying theta gives 2E(y) = D - X.

Step 5 (first relation; replaces the Zagier-Zinger citation). L2b P = 0: by (ii), with g_d = 3(H_{3d}-H_d), [(-y)^d] L2b h = 27(2d-1)a_{d-1} - 2d a_d. By the product rule L2b(A log y) = 2 Delta_c thetaA + 27yA, with coefficient 2d a_d - 27(2d-1)a_{d-1}. The sum is 0. Put W := A thetaP - P thetaA = A^2 D. Then theta W = -27yX W, so theta(Delta_c W) = 0. W = A^2 + A thetah - h thetaA is a log-free series with W(0) = 1. So Delta_c W = 1. QED.

Dictionary. With d2 := E(C1i^2-1)/(2 Delta_c) (Lemma 1.2 preamble) and c1 = A: Delta_c c1^2 = A^2/X = 1/D by the first relation, and d2 = (E/2)(X/A^2 - X) = (E/2)(D-X) = e_1(alpha*) E(y) by both relations. So Definition 1.3 at c1 = A is eq:RHb. [P]

=== PART II. AUDIT OF BS (reading of BS_v2 main.tex; not used by Theorems 1 and 3). ===

(a) eq:RHb [no dependence on either relation]. eq:SJ2 (2590) is pure GW axioms. eq:ssH1 (3077) is J=I. Divisor (3098) gives C^a_{1b} = A^{-1} theta s^a_b. (b) (Symplecticity) [no dependence]. eq:sympl (3083) follows by differentiation in t, using only eta-self-adjointness of the quantum product (symmetry of 3-point functions) and S = 1 + O(1/z). BS 3543 passes to R in one clause. The formal passage is: flatness and self-adjointness give (Y_i - Y_j + z theta) B_ij = 0 for B_ij := Sum R_ai(z) eta^ab R_bj(-z). This forces B_ij = 0 for i != j (induct in z, Y_i != Y_j) and theta B_ii = 0, and (Normalisation) with c_j odd in z gives B_ii = 1. No E(y) enters.

(c) Where modrel DOES enter BS downstream: printed eq:allc rows 2-4; eq:phi (Phi_2i through C^1_12, C^2_12); (Phi^-1)_{i1}; eq:XFABC (2857); eq:Sain and prop:fingenR (3349); 3856; 4836. BS's written derivation of Delta_i^{-1} = 1/(3 eps W_i) passes through these.

=== PART III. PROOF OF THEOREM 3. All steps [P] given Theorem A (draft s.2.1). ===

Setting. K := Q(eps1,eps2,omega)(t), y = t^3, theta = (t/3)d/dt. At colour i: Th_i = Y_i + z theta on K[[z]]. Put
  a := v_i S(v_i,z),  b := Th_i a,  c := Delta_c Th_i b.
Define 𝔅(u,w) := -(E^3/27)u_0w_0 + E u_1w_1 + u_1w_2 + u_2w_1, so eta^{ab} = -3 eps 𝔅. Let Pit_ij(z) := 𝔅((a,b,c)^{(i)}(z), (a,b,c)^{(j)}(-z)).

S0 (reduction; draft Prop 2.10 steps 1-2, re-verified by hand). For any c1, P_1 = C1i Q_1 and P_2 = C1i^{-1}[T - z Delta_c XX Q_1] - C1i(E/2)Q_1, with T = c' + (E/2)Q_1 in the notation below. The C1i^2 and XX terms cancel. With Q_1 = b/sqrt(c0), T = (c + (E/2) b)/sqrt(c0), c0 := 3 eps E, P_0 = a/sqrt(c0), the frame-B pairing equals -3 eps Pit_ij/c0 = -Pit_ij/E for every c1. The h_w factors give h_w(z)h_w(-z) = 1. So it suffices to prove Pit_ij = -E delta_ij.

S1 (first-order system). Conjugating eq:pf gives Delta_c Th^3 a + (E+27yz) Th^2 a + (E^2/3+6yz^2) Th a + (E^3/27) a = 0, which is Theorem A; (T = Th + alpha in its proof). Since Th(Delta_c f) = Delta_c Th f + 27yz f, the 27yz terms cancel:
  Th a = b,  Th b = c/Delta_c,  Th c = -(E/Delta_c) c - (E^2/3 + 6y z^2) b - (E^3/27) a.
The matrix depends on y and z^2 only, not on colour and not on the sign of z.

S2 (self-adjointness). With u, w satisfying this system:
  𝔅(Du,w) = -(E^3/27)(u_1w_0+u_0w_1) + u_2w_2/Delta_c - (E^2/3+6yz^2)u_1w_1,
because the terms E u_2w_1/Delta_c cancel. This is symmetric in u, w, hence equals 𝔅(u,Dw).

S3 (ODE). zθ u(z) = Th_i u - Y_i u. For w(-z), with Th_j(-z) = Y_j - zθ: zθ w = Y_j w - Th_j(-z) w. By S1 at z and at -z, and S2:
  (Y_i - Y_j + zθ) Pit_ij = 0.

S4 (i != j). Y_i - Y_j != 0 in K, and Pit_ij lies in K[[z]], so induction on the z-order gives Pit_ij = 0.

S5 (i = j). theta Pit_ii = 0, so each z-coefficient is constant in t. Colour i is the image of colour 0 under the field automorphism t -> omega^i t, which fixes y, Delta_c, theta. Hence Pit_ii = Pit_00 =: kappa(z) for all i.

S6 (the constant). Each [z^k] of a lies in v Q(eps)[v]. b = (1 - Ev/3)S + z(1/E - v/3)d_v(vS) lies in Q(eps)[v] at each z-order (theta v = 1/E - v/3). c = (Delta_c Y) b + Delta_c z theta b, with Delta_c Y = -(E/3)Delta_c + E t(1-3t+9t^2). All are regular at t = -1/3 (v_0 = 0, t = 1/(Ev-3)). There a = 0; b = S(0,z)(1 + z/E) = 1 since S(0,z) = E/(E+z); Delta_c = 0; Delta_c Y = -E; so c = -E. Thus kappa(z) = E·1·1 + 1·(-E) + (-E)·1 = -E, exactly in z. QED.

Since S(a l)S(b l) = a b l^2/(4 sinh(a l/2) sinh(b l/2)), we get [l^{2h}] S(e1 l)S(e2 l) = e1 e2 [l^{2h-2}] 1/(4 sinh sinh) = e1 e2 beta_{2h-2}(e)/(2h-3)!.
With sigma = -e1 e2 this turns R2 Cor 7 into sigma^h Int K Omega = -e1 e2 beta_{2h-2}(e) = sigma beta_{2h-2}(e), that is sigma^{h-1} Int K Omega = beta_{2h-2}(e).
Identification: PSM s.1.1(a) at r = 0 gives Sum_m (1/m!) pi_* prod T(psi_k) = exp(Sum_k kappa_k [z^k](-log(1 - T(z)/z))) = exp(-Sum kappa_k/k) = K, because 1 - T(z)/z = 1/(1-z). Hence Int K Omega = Fpot_h(q_0)|_{c=1} = Z_h.
Homogenisation: (7.2) at r = 0 gives Z[h,0] = E^{-(3h-3)} Z_h. Also -eps1 eps2 E^3 = sigma E^5 and beta_n(lambda a, lambda b) = lambda^n beta_n(a,b). So (-eps1 eps2 E^3)^{h-1} Z[h,0] = sigma^{h-1} E^{5h-5-3h+3} Z_h = E^{2h-2} beta_{2h-2}(e) = beta_{2h-2}(eps).
This replaces the [E] gap_identity_check.pl claim. The same conversion applies to the theorem proved below, so Part B can be used with or without R2.

PART B. Independent all-genus proof of (VI). It replaces the ABDKS/Eynard route, so the normalisation behind R2 is no longer needed.

Notation: e := 1+tau; sigma' = 1+2 tau; M_h(1^a) := <Omega prod_{i=1}^a 1/(1-psi_i)>_{h,a}; G_h(y) := Sum_a M_h(1^a) y^a/a!. In genus 1 the sum starts at a = 1. M_0(1^a) := a^{a-3}, the LLZ unstable convention.

Step 1 [C LLZ eq. (1)-(3); the conversion is P]. The MV formula in real form, for all g and all mu.
LLZ state: Sum_{mu,g} lambda^{2g-2+l} C_{g,mu} p_mu = log Sum_nu e^{i(tau+1/2) kappa_nu lambda/2} V_nu(lambda) s_nu(p), with C_{g,mu} = -(i^{|mu|+l}/|Aut mu|) sigma^{l-1} Pi_mu I_g(mu), I_g(mu) = Int Lambda^vee(1)Lambda^vee(-tau-1)Lambda^vee(tau)/prod(1-mu_i psi_i), and V_nu = prod_box 1/(2 sin(h lambda/2)).
Put x = i lambda. Then 2 sin(h lambda/2) = -i 2 sinh(h x/2), so V_nu = i^{|nu|} prod_box (2 sinh(hx/2))^{-1}, and i^{|nu|} s_nu(p) = s_nu(i^k p_k).
On the left, lambda^{2g-2+l} (-i^{|mu|+l}) = (-1)^g i^{|mu|} x^{2g-2+l}. Cancelling i^{|mu|} and using I_g = (-sigma)^g M_g gives, with Z(p) := Sum_nu e^{(tau+1/2) kappa_nu x/2} prod_box (2 sinh(hx/2))^{-1} s_nu(p) and F := log Z:
  [x^{2g-2+l} p_mu] F = sigma^{g+l-1} Pi_mu M_g(mu)/|Aut mu|.   (1.1)
This derivation also settles, for all genera, the normalisation that critic 1 S1 flags on the p_1 slice, and the general mu form is the same computation.
By the principal specialisation (Macdonald I.3 Ex. 2), s_nu(q^rho) = q^{kappa_nu/4}/prod_box [h] with [h] = q^{h/2} - q^{-h/2}, q = e^x. Hence Z = Sum_nu e^{tau x f_2(nu)} s_nu(q^rho) s_nu(p), f_2 = kappa/2.
On the slice p = (p_1, 0, 0, ...), set p_1 = y/(sigma x). Then (1.1) gives
  F = Sum_{h>=0} sigma^{h-1} x^{2h-2} (G_h(y) - G_h(0))   in Q(tau)[[y]]((x)).   (1.2)
There is no a = 0 term on the Schur side, since Z(0) = 1. That constant plays no role below.

Step 2 [P, with C for the boson-fermion dictionary]. A closed equation on the p_1 slice.
(a) Cut-and-join, by eigenvalues. Let C := (1/2) Sum_{i,j} (i j p_{i+j} d_i d_j + (i+j) p_i p_j d_{i+j}), d_i = d/dp_i. Then C s_nu = f_2(nu) s_nu, which is LLZ Thm 1 in Schur form and standard (test: C p_1^2 = p_2, C p_2 = p_1^2). So dZ/dtau = x C Z. Restricting log Z to the slice gives
  d_tau F|_p = x p_1^2 d_2 F.
(b) First mKP. With t_k = p_k/k and g = e^{tau x F_2} Gamma_-(p'), p'_k = 1/[k], put tau_n(t) := <n|Gamma_+(t) g|n> (half-integer modes, |n> filled below n). The charge-n eigenvalue of F_2 on |nu,n> is f_2(nu) + n|nu| + C(n), so tau_0 = Z and tau_1 = e^{tau x/8} Z(e^{k beta} p_k) with beta := tau x.
Since (A⊗1 + 1⊗A) commutes with Sum_k psi_k ⊗ psi_k^* for bilinear A, and Sum_k psi_k|1> ⊗ psi_k^*|0> = 0 (psi_k|1> = 0 for k < 1, psi_k^*|0> = 0 for k > 0), we get Sum_k psi_k g|1> ⊗ psi_k^* g|0> = 0. The vertex-operator form of psi, psi^* then gives Res_z z e^{xi(t-t',z)} tau_1(t-[1/z]) tau_0(t'+[1/z]) dz = 0 [C: boson-fermion correspondence; Date-Jimbo-Kashiwara-Miwa; Miwa-Jimbo-Date, Solitons]. Setting t = a+b, t' = a-b, b = 0 gives h_2(-D~) tau_1.tau_0 = 0, that is
  (D_1^2 - D_2) tau_1.tau_0 = 0.
The form is derived, not fitted. A hand test at degree 2 with p' = (c, 0, ...) gives (c^2/2)[e^{3b} + e^{b} - 4e^{b} + e^{b} + e^{-b} - e^{3b} + e^{b} + e^{b} - e^{-b}] = 0, and flipping D_2 breaks it.
In logs, with F1(p) = F(e^{k beta} p_k):
  2 d_2(F - F1) + d_1^2 (F + F1) + (d_1(F - F1))^2 = 0.
(c) Eliminate d_2. On the slice d_2 F1 = e^{2 beta} (d_2 F)(e^beta p_1), and (a) gives d_2 F(P) = d_tau F(P)/(x P^2), so the e^{2 beta} cancels. With D := y d_y = p_1 d_{p_1}, multiply by p_1^2:
  (2/x)(1 - e^{beta D}) F_tau + (D^2 - D)(1 + e^{beta D}) F + ((1 - e^{beta D}) D F)^2 = 0,   (*)
where F_tau := d_tau|_p F = (d_tau|_y + (sigma'/sigma) D) F, because y = sigma x p_1.
(*) is an exact identity in Q(tau)[[y]]((x)). It contains F only through DF and through D-derivatives of F_tau, so constants in y are irrelevant.

Step 3 [P, given string and dilaton for pull-back classes]. The dilaton point.
Lambda classes pull back under forgetful maps. For h >= 2 put FF(c,p,r) := Sum_m (1/m!) <Omega prod(c + r psi + p/(1-psi))(psi_i)>_{h,m}. String and dilaton read (1-r) d_c FF = p d_p FF and (1-r) d_r FF = (2h-2 + c d_c + p d_p) FF. Hence FF(c,p,r) = (1-r)^{2-2h} G_h((p/(1-r)) e^{c/(1-r)}).
Since psi^2/(1-psi) = 1/(1-psi) - 1 - psi, taking (c,p,r) = (-s, s, -s) gives Q_h(s) := Sum_k (s^k/k!) <Omega (psi^2/(1-psi))^k>, and
  G_h(y) = w^{2h-2} Q_h(w-1),   w := 1+s = 1/(1-u),   y = u e^{-u}.
Q_h has degree <= 3h-3 and Q_h(-1) = Z_h. So G_h = w^{2h-2}(Z_h + O(w)), a polynomial in w. Also D = (w-1) w^2 d_w; with v := 1/w this is D = (1 - 1/v) d_v.
Genus 0: D^2 G_0 = Sum a^{a-1} y^a/a! = u = 1-v, hence G_0 = 5/12 - v^2/4 - v^3/6.
Genus 1: with a marked leg 1/(1-psi_0) the same PDEs give DG_1 = u w Q_1(s;(1)), where Q_1(s;(1)) = Int_{1,1}(psi + Omega_1) + s<tau_2 tau_0>_1 = (s - 1/sigma)/24 (on genus 1, Omega = 1 - ((1+sigma)/sigma) lambda_1). So DG_1 = (w-1)(w-1-1/sigma)/24, i.e. G_1 = (1/24)(-log v + (1+1/sigma) v) + const.
Every x-coefficient of DF is a Laurent polynomial in w, and Laurent polynomials embed in Q(tau)[[y]] because w = 1 + y + ... is non-constant. So (*) holds coefficientwise in the monomials x^a w^b.

Step 4 [P]. Grading.
Map x^a w^b to eps^{b-a} N^{-b}, with eps = 1/x and v = xN. Each coefficient has a unique preimage, and N-powers are bounded above at fixed eps-order. Then D = eps(1 - eps/N) d_N and beta D = tau(1 - eps/N) d_N is a derivation, so e^{beta D} f(N) = f(Phi) with dPhi/dtau = 1 - eps/Phi. Hence e^{beta D} = E + eps E_1 + O(eps^2), where E f(N) = f(M), M := N + tau, and E_1 f = -l f'(M), l := log(M/N). Put Delta := E - 1. By (1.2) and Step 3, modulo constants in y,
  F = x A + B + eps C + ...,
  A = -N^3/(6 sigma) + a N, a = (1+sigma)/(24 sigma),
  B = -N^2/(4 sigma) - (1/24) log N + B_s,   B_s := Sum_{h>=2} sigma^{h-1} Z_h N^{2-2h}.
Here d_tau is taken at fixed N.
Inserting into (*):
Order eps^0: -2 Delta A_tau - (1+E) A' + (Delta A')^2 = 0. This holds identically and is a check: the N^2, N^1 and N^0 coefficients each vanish, the last only because of a.
Order eps^1: C does not enter, and
  -2 Delta(B_tau + (sigma'/sigma) A') - 2 E_1 A_tau + (1+E)A'' + (1/N)(1+E)A' - (1+E)B' - d_N E_1 A + 2 (Delta A') [Delta(B' - A'/N) + E_1 A'] = 0.
Use Delta A' = -(M+N)/(2e). The pieces are:
  coefficient of l: 2A_tau'(M) + A''(M) - 2 Delta A' A''(M) = (MN - sigma'/12)/sigma^2;
  remaining source terms: -tau(M+N)/(2 sigma^2) + (a/e)(1/M + 1/N);
  the -N^2/(4 sigma) and -(1/24) log N parts of B contribute (1/(24 e))(1/M + 1/N).
With L[B] := -2 Delta B_tau - (1+E) B' - ((M+N)/e) Delta B', this gives
  L[B_s] = (1/sigma^2) { -l (MN - sigma'/12) + tau (M+N)/2 - (tau (1+2 sigma)/24) (1/M + 1/N) }.   (E1)
Note a + 1/24 = (1+2 sigma)/(24 sigma) and sigma/e = tau. (E1) involves only the Z_h, no other unknown.

Step 5 [P]. Solving (E1).
Let LL: Q(tau)[[t]] -> N^{-1} Q(tau)[[1/N]], t^k -> k! N^{-k-1}, a bijection. Checking on monomials gives: LL[e^{-tau t} phi] = E LL[phi]; N LL[phi] = phi(0) + LL[phi_t]; d_N LL[phi] = -LL[t phi]; LL[(1-e^{-tau t})/t] = l.
Set P := 1 - e^{-tau t}, so that P_t = tau(1-P) and 2 P_t + tau P = tau(2-P). Write B_s = LL[f_s/t] with f_s := Sum_{h>=2} sigma^{h-1} Z_h t^{2h-2}/(2h-3)!. Then L[LL[f/t]] = LL[LLop f] for f in t^2 Q(tau)[[t]], where
  LLop f := 2P (f_tau/t - f_t/e) + (2-P) f/e.
For the right side of (E1): with phi = P/t, MN l - tau(M+N)/2 = LL[phi_tt + tau phi_t] = LL[2P/t^3 - tau(2-P)/t^2], a regular series. Also 1/M + 1/N = LL[2-P].
Apply the formula LLop to f_sing := -1/(sigma t^2) + d, d := (1+2 sigma)/(24 sigma). Using d_tau(-1/sigma) + 2(-1/sigma)/e = 1/sigma^2 and d_tau d = -sigma'/(24 sigma^2) gives
  LLop f_sing = (1/sigma^2) [2P/t^3 - tau(2-P)/t^2 - (sigma'/12) P/t + (tau(1+2 sigma)/24)(2-P)],
which is exactly minus the Borel preimage of the right side of (E1). Since LL is injective, (E1) is equivalent to
  LLop(f_sing + f_s) = 0.
On the other side, f_* := 1/(4 sinh(e1 t/2) sinh(e2 t/2)) = -1/(4 sinh(tau t/2) sinh(e t/2)) satisfies f_*,tau/(t f_*) - f_*,t/(e f_*) = -coth(tau t/2)/(2e). Therefore LLop f_* = (f_*/e)[-P coth(tau t/2) + 2 - P] = 0, because P coth(tau t/2) = 1 + e^{-tau t} = 2 - P.
Also f_* = f_sing + f_reg with f_reg = Sum_{h>=2} beta_{2h-2}(e1,e2) t^{2h-2}/(2h-3)!, since e1 e2 = -sigma and e1^2 + e2^2 = 1 + 2 sigma.
So W := f_s - f_reg in t^2 Q(tau)[[t]] satisfies LLop W = 0.
Uniqueness: suppose W = w_n t^n + ... with w_n != 0 and n >= 2. The t^n coefficient of LLop W gives tau w_n' - (n tau - 1) w_n/e = 0, so w_n = C tau^{-1} (1+tau)^{n+1}. But W is invariant under tau -> -1-tau: sigma and Omega are, since the weights tau and -1-tau swap, and f_reg is, since e1 and e2 swap. Invariance forces C[(1+tau)^{n+2} - (-1)^n tau^{n+2}] = 0, hence C = 0. So W = 0, that is sigma^{h-1} Z_h = beta_{2h-2}(e1, e2) for every h >= 2. QED for Theorem VI at c = 1. Part A's homogenisation then gives (VI).

Sanity limits, not used in the proof: tau -> oo gives Int K Lambda^vee(1) = B_{2h}/(2h(2h-2)) = chi(M_h) (Harer-Zagier, consistent with PSM s.1.1(c)). tau -> 0 gives Int lambda_h K = -(2h-3)! b_h, the lambda_g value in Route A s.2.4 at j = 0.

Theorem VI. Work at c = 1: w = (1, tau, -1-tau), sigma = tau(1+tau), Omega = Lambda^vee(1) Lambda^vee(tau) Lambda^vee(-1-tau)/(-sigma)^h, T = -psi^2/(1-psi), e1 = -tau, e2 = 1+tau. Let Z_h(tau) := Fpot_h(q_0) = Sum_m (1/m!) <Omega prod T(psi_k)>_{h,m} (= Int_{Mbar_h} K Omega). Then for every h >= 2, identically in tau,

  sigma^{h-1} Z_h(tau) = beta_{2h-2}(e1, e2), where beta_n(a,b) := (n-1)! [t^n] 1/(4 sinh(a t/2) sinh(b t/2)).

Equivalently, sigma^h Z_h = -(2h-3)! [l^{2h}] S(e1 l) S(e2 l) with S(y) = (y/2)/sinh(y/2) (this is R2 Cor 7). In homogeneous form, for E = eps1 + eps2 and tau = -eps1/E, (-eps1 eps2 E^3)^{h-1} Z[h,0] = beta_{2h-2}(eps1, eps2), which is (VI).

The proof is new. It is uniform in h and uses no TR, no Eynard/ABDKS, no Lemma A, no Teleman and no finite-order input. It combines the Marino-Vafa formula, the first mKP equation and the cut-and-join eigenvalue on the p_1-slice, then extracts the lowest order at the dilaton point. The tau-symmetry of Omega fixes the integration constants.
